unit: Students can describe their daily study routines, discuss learning tools, and share advice for building good study habits while balancing school and family life.
objective: Discuss what to do before a school test.

title: Warm-up
subtitle: Getting ready for a test
question: How do you usually review your notes and memorize facts before a big test?
starters: Before a big test, I usually...
To help me memorize facts, I try to...

title: Useful Language (Part 1)
teacher_instructions: Read each word aloud and have the student repeat it.
Read the definition and example sentence.
Ask the check question to confirm understanding.
Ask the student to make their own sentence using one of the words.

words.definition: To succeed on a test or exam by getting a good score.
words.example: I need to study hard so I can pass my English test.
words.check: What is the best way to pass a test: guessing the answers or reviewing your notes?

words.definition: To get a low score and not pass a test or exam.
words.example: If you don't study, you might fail the exam.
words.check: What usually happens if you fail a test: do you have to take it again, or do you get a prize?

title: Useful language (part 2)
teacher_instructions: Read each word aloud and ask the student to repeat it.
Read the definition and the example sentence.
Ask the check questions to confirm understanding.
Ask the student to make their own sentence using one of the words.

words.definition: to do something many times so that you get better at it
words.example: I need to practice speaking English every day.
words.check: What is something you practice every week: speaking English or playing a sport?

words.definition: to learn something carefully so that you can remember it exactly
words.example: It's important to memorize these new words.
words.check: Which is easier to memorize: a short song or a long book?

words.definition: an important test, usually taken at school
words.example: I have a big math exam tomorrow.
words.check: How do you usually feel before an exam: nervous or calm?

title: Conversation Builder
goal: Learn how to talk about things you must do before an exam.

linkers.use: Say an action is important for you.

model:
Tutor: What should we do to pass the big exam? 
Student: Well, I have to memorize my notes, and I need to practice the test questions. 
Tutor: Good point. Is there anything else? 
Student: Yeah, it is important to go to bed early.

your_turn.teacher: Ask the student: I have an exam tomorrow. What should I do so I don't fail?
your_turn.student: Give advice using: I have to... / I need to... / It is important to...

title: Let's practice
teacher_question: Imagine I'm your classmate. I have a big exam tomorrow, and I'm really worried I'll fail. Tell me what you do to review your notes and memorize facts.
student_guide: Well, I usually need to _____ before an exam.

title: Real-world scenario
problem: Your classmate has a big exam tomorrow. They are worried about failing and need your help.
mission: Tell your classmate what they need to do to pass the exam.
Give them advice on how to practice and memorize their notes.
Use phrases like: 'It is important to...'
start: Hey, I'm so worried about our exam tomorrow! What do I need to do to pass?

title: Wrap-Up
recap: Vocabulary: pass, fail, practice, memorize, exam
Chunks: I have to... / I need to... / It is important to...
Skill: You practiced giving advice on how to prepare for a big school test.
final_task: Using today's phrases, tell me in one sentence: What is one thing you must do to pass an exam?
challenge: Next time you study, try using the words 'memorize' and 'practice' to describe your routine.
